metaTitle: About Barwon Asbestos Co | Asbestos Testing, Removal and Disposal in Geelong and the Barwon Region
metaDescription: We take the samples, a NATA-accredited lab analyses them, and licensed Victorian removalists quote the work. How we scope an asbestos job around Geelong.
heroSub: We are the step before the removalist. We take the samples, a NATA-accredited laboratory does the analysis, and licensed Victorian removalists quote the removal themselves, for homeowners across Geelong, the Bellarine, the Surf Coast and Golden Plains.
storyHtml:
Most people find us in the middle of a problem. A fence has cracked along the back boundary, a garage roof has started to break up, or a renovation has stopped because nobody can say what the sheeting is. We don't hold a removal licence and we don't claim one: we take samples, have them analysed, and put you in touch with licensed asbestos removalists who quote and carry out the work themselves. You contract with them directly, and their WorkSafe Victoria licence number is on the quote.

Diagnosis starts with the material, not the house. Every different material is its own sample, so a fence, an eaves lining and a bathroom wall sheet are three tests rather than one, and most houses need three to eight. Victoria's OHS Regulations allow only a laboratory approved by NATA to identify asbestos in a sample, which means nobody's eye counts, including ours. Analysis runs $88 to $160 per sample and results usually come back in one to five business days, and our asbestos testing page sets out the whole process.

Once the result is in, two things set the scope: whether the material is friable, and how much of it there is. Nearly all residential fibro around Geelong is non-friable and falls to a Class B licence holder, including fence lines, Super Six roofing, eaves and shed cladding. Friable material, such as pipe lagging or sheeting that is crumbling or fire damaged, is Class A work at any quantity, with no exemption for small amounts. Quantity decides the rest: 10 square metres and one hour in any seven days are the limits the law sets for anyone doing this as work, and a full fence line or a garage roof is well past both.

A quote reads better when you know what belongs on it. The minimum job charge, $800 to $1,500 in Victoria, is the reason a two-sheet repair costs what it does. A clearance certificate, which is required once the job passes 10 square metres of non-friable material, sits on its own line at $165 to $250, because the person who issues one has to be independent of the removalist, and disposal is a separate cost again, since the waste can only go to a landfill authorised to receive it and Drysdale is the only one in the Barwon region. Those are published Victorian figures rather than our prices, and the rest of them sit on our asbestos removal cost page.

values.title: Get it tested before you touch it
values.desc: Testing is the cheap step and the honest one. Lab analysis is $88 to $160 a sample, and a negative result ends the matter before anyone spends money on removal. A positive one tells you what you are actually dealing with, in writing.

values.title: A sample for every material
values.desc: Fibro cladding, an eaves lining and a vinyl floor tile are three materials and three separate results. Most houses need three to eight samples, and a larger property can run to eight or twelve. Judging a whole house from one sheet is how a scope goes wrong.

values.title: Friable or not, and how much of it
values.desc: Those two answers decide who is allowed to do the work. Non-friable fibro is Class B, friable material is Class A at any quantity, and the 10 square metre and one hour caps that bind anyone doing this as work are why a fence line or a roof is never a weekend job.

values.title: Clear about what we are not
values.desc: We hold no licence, we don't run or supervise the removal, and we don't price the work that follows it. A new fence, new cladding or a new roof is a separate job with a registered builder. Every figure on this site comes from published Victorian rates, not from us.

faq.a: No, and we never say otherwise. Removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists we work with, and their WorkSafe Victoria licence number appears on every quote. We are not NATA accredited either: that accreditation belongs to the laboratory that analyses the sample. The same logic runs through the whole job, since the person who issues a clearance certificate has to be independent of the removalist and of whoever commissioned the work.

faq.q: So what do you actually do?
faq.a: We take samples and a NATA-accredited laboratory analyses them, usually back within one to five business days. We explain what the report says in plain terms, and if asbestos is detected we put you in touch with licensed removalists who quote the job themselves. From there you deal with them directly, and when the work is at your own home and you engaged the licence holder, the duty to obtain the clearance certificate sits with them rather than with you.

faq.q: Why don't you publish your own prices?
faq.a: Because they would not be ours to publish. The ranges on this site are what Victorian suppliers and councils publish, mostly on a Melbourne-metro basis, since nobody publishes a Geelong or Barwon rate for this work. GST treatment varies between providers too, so ask each removalist whether their quote includes GST.
